# INGV earthquake catalogue (ISIDe)

`ingv_catalog` · adapter 1.0.0 · makes `seismic_catalog` tokens

| | |
|---|---|
| Provider | Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia (INGV), Rome |

## Terms

ISIDe data are licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International. Use them freely and cite the database.

## Cite

- ISIDe Working Group (2007). Italian Seismological Instrumental and Parametric Database (ISIDe). Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia (INGV). https://doi.org/10.13127/ISIDE

## Access

FDSN event service `https://webservices.ingv.it/fdsnws/event/1/query`, `format=text`, one request per calendar month inside the region's box. The service refuses requests over 20,000 events (HTTP 413); such months are fetched in halves and joined under one header. At most one request per second; every month is downloaded once and cached by hash, and only `craton data fetch --refresh` asks again.

## From the source to the token

| Token slot | Comes from |
|---|---|
| `kind` | `event` |
| `lat, lon` | Latitude, Longitude |
| `depth_km` | Depth/Km (below sea level; under 0.11 km from the ellipsoid, D-012) |
| `time` | Time, UTC |
| `value` | Magnitude |
| `qualifiers` | magnitude_type ← MagType, event_id ← EventID, event_type |
| `provenance.record` | `eventid=<EventID>;author=<Author>` |
| `provenance.content_hash` | sha256 of the month's raw file |

## Uncertainty

The text service publishes no errors. Magnitude 1σ is assumed: 0.1 for Mw, 0.2 for ML, 0.3 for every other type (`uncertainty_basis: assumed`). Location errors are absent, so `resolution` is an assumed 1 km and 0.1 s, and `location_uncertainty` is left out.

## Known issues

- Magnitude types are mixed: mostly ML, some Md (older years) and Mw. Every token carries its type; nothing converts between them.
- The magnitude of completeness changes with time and with the network; it drops sharply after the 2000s and rises right after big shocks. The health report estimates it per year.
- Since 2005 the bulletin reviews only M ≥ 1.5; smaller events stay as the automatic or survey locations (`author` in the record says which).
- Events from 1985 to April 2005 were added to the service years after it went online; their locations come from older procedures and are less precise.
- INGV revises recent months. A refresh brings new bytes, a new hash and new tokens; the old version stays in the raw store.
- Event types other than earthquake, induced event, quarry blast and explosion are refused and counted, never guessed.
